alerts.alertName: Mimikatz credential theft tool (Blocked LSASS credential dumping attempt)
alerts.whatTriggered: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint has identified a high-severity credential access alert after detecting HackTool:Win32/Mimikatz.I in a PowerShell command attempting to download Mimikatz and run sekurlsa::logonpasswords. Defender reports it was blocked and succesfully remediated. The alert is linked to incident #95, with SandCat activity and a subsequent blocked ProcDump/LSASS attempt in the same alert story.
alerts.whyTriggered:
Defender identifies the detection source as **Antivirus**, service as **Microsoft Defender for Endpoint**, and technology as **Client,Heuristic**. The reported threat is `HackTool:Win32/Mimikatz.I`, with detection status **Blocked**. The command includes `privilege::debug and sekurlsa::logonpasswords`, consistent with an attempt to read credentials from LSASS.

This is the observed vendor detection result and an interpretation of the PowerShell command; the underlying signature or exact heuristic rule was not exposed. The alert-level MITRE field is blank.
alerts.whatHappened:
***Observed sequence***
The process tree shows wininit.exe (PID 688) → services.exe (PID 816) → nssm.exe (PID 5092) → wusvc.exe (PID 1928). The latter two ran with System integrity under NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM. The service ancestors started on 21 March; their presence alone does not establish when compromise began.

On 12 June 2026 at 16:45:11, C:\Users\Public\wusvc.exe ran with `-server hxxp://172.31.2[.]203:8888 -group red.` Defender associated it with Trojan:Win64/SandCat.RTS!MTB. This is a configured server address in the command line, not independently verified network traffic.

At 17:20:44, the alert story records prevention of a PowerShell command that stages a Mimikatz archive in %TEMP%\svcdiag, extracts it and attempts privilege::debug followed by sekurlsa::logonpasswords. At 17:;21:28, a second command attempts to use ProcDump against lsass.exe, targeting %TEMP%\svctools\lsass.dmp. Defender reports both attempts blocked, with remove remediation returning Success.
alerts.queries:
No KQL queries were executed for this report.
Investigation used the Defender alert details, expanded process tree, remediation fields, comments and history, and recommendations.
